title: Ski school - Azure logical flow

azurerm_resource_group.global.label: Global Front Door RG | infra/frontdoor | global edge

azurerm_group.backend_state.label: infra/backend | separate state, NOT another RG

azurerm_resource_group.global.title: Global Front Door RG
azurerm_resource_group.global.detail: Owns the global Front Door profile, endpoint, routes and diagnostics. The diagram shows one frontend origin, which remains publicly reachable.

azurerm_resource_group.frontend.title: Frontend RG
azurerm_resource_group.frontend.detail: Owns one Container App and its Container Apps environment. The bridge uses the app's system-assigned identity to invoke the agent; a separate identity pulls container images. Its origin check is not caller authentication.

azurerm_resource_group.foundry.title: Foundry RG
azurerm_resource_group.foundry.detail: Contains the Foundry account, project, model deployments and Application Insights. The project identity pulls agent images; the agent has a separate runtime identity. Model and hosted-agent support and quota must be verified for the target region.

azurerm_resource_group.gateway.title: Gateway RG
azurerm_resource_group.gateway.detail: Owns AI Gateway and its routing, MCP policy and telemetry configuration. The agent uses scoped identity grants to call Gateway; Gateway's system identity needs access to Foundry. Regional support must be verified; the diagram does not establish live availability or failover.

azurerm_resource_group.registry.title: Registry RG
azurerm_resource_group.registry.detail: Owns the container registry. The frontend image-pull identity and Foundry project identity receive separate pull permissions; neither is the image publishing identity.

azurerm_resource_group.logging.title: Logging RG
azurerm_resource_group.logging.detail: Owns Log Analytics and Azure Monitor workspaces as telemetry destinations. Resource-group metadata and workspace locations can differ; verify regional compatibility for telemetry. Configured connections do not prove successful ingestion.

step_details: The browser accesses the global Front Door hostname over HTTPS. The Container App also has public ingress; Front Door is not the only possible entry point. The diagram shows one frontend origin, not regional failover.
Front Door routes over HTTPS to the frontend. nginx serves the JavaScript website and forwards /api/ requests to the Python bridge in the same app.

The bridge validates the request origin, JSON and chat history, then uses the Container App's system-assigned identity to obtain an Entra token and call the hosted agent's Responses API. Origin validation is not caller authentication.

The hosted Microsoft Agent Framework agent uses an OpenAI-compatible client against Gateway. Its runtime identity obtains tokens for model and MCP calls, with separate scoped roles for the alias and tool server.
The agent requests the configured model alias. Gateway's system identity needs access to the Foundry account. Registered deployments and routing do not prove regional model availability or failover.

The agent discovers and invokes tools through the scoped Gateway MCP endpoint using its runtime identity. Gateway applies the configured tool policy and forwards permitted calls to the Foundry toolbox, whose backend must authorize the Gateway identity.

request.description: Configured request path; responses return along the calling path

steps.detail: Browser selects the edge hostname; the Container App also has public ingress.
Front Door routes to the frontend; nginx serves JavaScript and proxies /api/ to the bridge.
The bridge invokes the hosted agent with its system identity.
The Python MAF agent uses Gateway for model calls and MCP discovery/calls.
The model alias selects a configured Foundry deployment; there is no direct-model bypass.
The scoped MCP endpoint enforces tool policy and forwards to the versioned toolbox.
